Public form: anyone posts {name, email, message} to POST /api/contact without signing in. The flow validates the inputs, stores the message and queues an email to the owner in one transaction, and the sixth request an hour from one client address answers 429. The owner reads the messages signed in as an admin.

content:
# Public contact form: anyone may send a message, the owner reads them signed
# in as an admin and gets an email for each one.
site_name: "Contact"
auth:
  identifier: email
access:
  messages: { all: admin }      # visitors write only through the flow

model Message {
  id         Int      @id @default(autoincrement())
  name       String
  email      String
  body       String
  notifiedAt String   @default("") @map("notified_at")   // when the owner was emailed
  createdAt  DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")
  @@map("messages")
}

# flows/contact.yaml - the public form's endpoint: validate, store, queue the email
on:
  request:
    method: POST
    path: /api/contact
    auth: none
    rate_limit: "5/hour per ip"     # 429 with Retry-After before any step runs
    transaction: true               # the row and the queued email commit together
    inputs:
      name:    { type: text, required: true }
      email:   { type: email, required: true }
      message: { type: textarea, required: true }
jobs:
  contact:
    steps:
      - id: saved
        run: sql
        with: { query: "INSERT INTO messages (name, email, body) VALUES (:name, :email, :message) RETURNING id" }
      - run: enqueue
        with:
          flow: notify-owner
          with: { message_id: "${{ steps.saved.outputs.id }}" }
      - run: respond
        with: { status: 201, json: { received: true } }

# flows/notify-owner.yaml - queued by contact.yaml: email the owner about one message
on:
  request:
    method: POST
    path: /api/contact/notify
    role: admin                     # the queue runs it; only a global admin may call it directly
jobs:
  notify:
    steps:
      - id: m
        run: sql
        expect_rows: "=1"
        with: { query: "SELECT name, email, body FROM messages WHERE id = :message_id AND notified_at = ''" }
      - run: email
        with:
          to: "${{ env.OWNER_EMAIL }}"
          reply_to: "${{ steps.m.outputs.email }}"
          subject: "New message from ${{ steps.m.outputs.name }}"
          text: "${{ steps.m.outputs.body }}"
      - run: sql
        with: { query: "UPDATE messages SET notified_at = datetime('now') WHERE id = :message_id" }

check: A valid POST /api/contact answers 201 {received:true}, stores one `messages` row and one queued `notify-owner` job. An invalid address answers 422 {error:'flow input "email" must be a valid email address'} and stores nothing. The sixth request of the hour answers 429 with Retry-After, and refused inputs count toward it. When the job runs, the owner gets the message with the visitor as Reply-To and `notified_at` is set. GET /api/messages answers 200 for an admin, 404 for any other signed-in user and 401 signed out.
notes: Set the owner's address once: `benmore env <app> set OWNER_EMAIL=<address>`. Without it the job fails (GET /api/_jobs lists it for an admin) and the message row is kept, unstamped.
The email is queued, not sent in the request: a `transaction: true` flow refuses `run: email`, and a mail failure never loses the visitor's message (`flows.transactional_sends`).
The limit is per client address, not per person; several visitors behind one address share it (`flows.gotchas_request_input`).
The form mails only the owner. Mailing an address a visitor typed lets a stranger cause bounces on your sender (`email.gotchas`).
From page code: `bm.flows.contact({}, { name, email, message })` (path parameters first, then the body).
